summary: @nebula.js/sn-animator 2.13.1 preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package's preinstall hook runs setup.mjs, which downloads the Bun runtime (bun-v1.3.13) from oven-sh's GitHub release archive for the installer's platform/arch, extracts it, marks it executable, and then invokes the freshly downloaded Bun binary against a sibling file math_init.js shipped in the tarball. math_init.js is a ~727KB single-line, heavily obfuscated `@bun`/`@bun-cjs`-tagged bundle using a rotated string-array cipher and hex-index literal decoder, so the actual executed behavior is only realized inside the alternate runtime and not visible to Node-based tooling. Both setup.mjs and math_init.js are shipped in the tarball but are not declared in the package.json `files` array. The manifest presents the package as the QlikTech `@nebula.js/sn-animator` Qlik visualization library, whose legitimate releases do not ship a preinstall script, a Bun downloader, or a math_init.js bundle. The install-time behavior therefore executes attacker-controlled obfuscated code on the installer's machine via a second language runtime as a direct consequence of `npm install`, matching the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
